decisionQuestion: Where does the release line live on the Build board so a reader finds it, it keeps a fixed height, and it stays independent of the finished-card strip?
jobImportance: high — the reader's whole reason for opening the board is to know what needs them and what shipped; an unfindable line answers neither

fixedConstraints.name: one fixed-height line plus a slide-over
fixedConstraints.value: The board carries one line; the last five releases per project live in a slide-over, not inline

fixedConstraints.name: never an inline expander
fixedConstraints.value: The expansion must not push the kanban down
fixedConstraints.source: spec-product_v2 solution section; flow-strip.tsx docstring records the reported bug

fixedConstraints.name: independent of the finished-card count
fixedConstraints.value: A project with releases and no finished cards must still see its line

fixedConstraints.name: releases only, never card counts
fixedConstraints.value: The surface reports releases; the flow strip owns finished cards

fixedConstraints.name: surface must exist on the Build board
fixedConstraints.value: Mounted where the flow strip already mounts

criteria: a reader who has never opened it finds the line without being told
the line costs the kanban no vertical space it cannot spare
the release reading cannot be confused with the finished-card reading
every absence state is visible from the line, not only inside the slide-over
relatedDimensions: touch target size on a narrow screen

evidence.claim: The flow strip returns null when the finished-card count is zero, so anything sharing its guard disappears for a project with releases and no finished cards
A right-side slide-over already exists and is the flow strip's own expansion pattern, so the plan's expansion choice reuses tested machinery
The flow strip mounts above the kanban on the Build board, which is the band a placement decision has to work with
Five reviewers independently found the board's vertical budget and the flow strip's empty guard to be the two facts that break a naive placement
The reader chose a slide-over over a tab inside the flow surface, and a fleet line that states the newest release plus how many projects shipped

scopeCoverage.note: Own component, own line, own slide-over.
Needs FlowStrip's count===0 early return changed before it can show anything for a project without finished cards.
Findability is the cost; the line itself is unchanged.

options.primaryValue: zero height with a named entry

scopeCoverage.note: Independent surface with no shared guard.

missingInputs: no screenshot or live measurement of the board's vertical budget at 360 px / laptop height, so the height cost of A is argued rather than measured
acceptedSacrifice: Whichever placement is picked, the other three stop existing; the line's content, its slide-over and its absence sentences are unaffected by the choice.
nextAction: Show these four directions at the interface gate and stop for the reader's pick.
